items.title: The dependency-vetting check triggers on workflow action references
body: The security-hygiene.dependency-vetting deterministic trigger keys on package manifests only, so a diff adding googleapis/release-please-action@v5.0.0 — third-party code running with contents:write — showed 'not triggered' and the batch 11 T3 reviewer had to file the missing vetting record by hand.

Fix: extend the trigger — a diff that adds or changes a `uses:` reference under .github/workflows/ requires dependency_vetting with the workflow file in manifests and the action reference in dependencies. Requires the owner's ruling first: the check lives on a STANDING entry (both knowledge copies) and the runner change lives in crates/houserules/src/rules/audit.rs's `run_check` (batch 20 T3 retired template/tools/kb.mjs, the runner's pre-rewrite home).
Source: batch 11 branch review, violated_rules 2 and template_defects 2 (2026-09-03). Standing-entry change: OWNER RULING PENDING, listed in the batch 11 report.

items.title: Modular installs: adopters choose the feature set
body: Owner intent recorded at the Tier-2 CLI-surface ruling (2026-09-04): houserules becomes modular — an adopter can install only backlog management, or rules management without the backlog, or the full kit. This is WHY the flat command surface keeps per-module checks (check-knowledge, check-backlog) and the Rust crate separates rules, backlog, and install modules.

Shape: a feature/selection mechanism in init (and update honoring it) that installs a subset of the payload — the seeded files, generated artifacts, skills, and checks scoped to the chosen modules; the stamp records the selection. Details to the batch spec when gated, AFTER the Tier-2 port completes (the port ships everything; the crate boundaries prepare the split).
Source: owner, 2026-09-04, at the batch 15 CLI-surface ruling; the Tier-2 spec's architecture section carries the boundary design.

items.title: Default starter rule set: docs and code-quality style adopters begin with
body: Owner intent (2026-09-04): adopters should start with a curated default set of rules — docs style and code-quality style in tag-pilot's vein — instead of a near-empty seed. Today template/knowledge/ ships 36 entries that are process-heavy (23 process entries) while quality carries 2 and writing-style 3; no docs-style or language-agnostic code-quality starter content exists.

Shape: curate a default entry set for the quality and writing-style topics (and a docs area if warranted), modeled on the tag-pilot checkout's rules as a READ-ONLY reference (houserules.tag-pilot-is-read-only). Content work, independent of the Tier-2 binary; interacts with HR-053 (a starter set is what a modular rules-only install would seed). Curation choices and any new areas go to the batch spec when gated.
Source: owner, 2026-09-04, mid batch 16.

items.title: Capture-file citations for oversized report evidence
body: Batch 16 branch review, template defect 1: task-4-report.json reached 583KB because all 41 tdd entries embed verbatim RED/GREEN inline; reviewers re-ran cycles anyway, and T5's fix round already invented the better shape (bulk evidence in named workspace files, byte-prefix-matching inline excerpts).

Change: let a tdd or live_run entry cite a workspace capture file by path for output beyond a stated size, keeping the first lines plus exit inline; standardize the t5-evidence/ convention in .claude/schemas/deliverables.json and both agent templates. Deferred from batch 16 because template changes trigger process.evals-rerun and the batch was already closing.
Source: batch 16 branch review retrospective, 2026-09-04.

items.title: kb audit: an explicit empty-range mode
body: Batch 16 branch review, template defect 2: T5's three empty-range audits (research task, no diff) produced three byte-identical near-vacuous files — every deterministic row passes trivially and none speaks to the actual deliverable; the schema still demands self_audit, so the ritual ran three times for no signal.

Change: give audit an explicit empty-range mode that says so in one summary row (it already emits empty_range: true), and let a research task's report point its evidence rows at the workspace doc instead of the diff. Ships in template/tools until the Tier-2 port owns audit (phase 2), then carries into the Rust audit.
Source: batch 16 branch review retrospective, 2026-09-04.

items.title: Narrow check-report-claims' paste-run lint: quote-aware placeholder, $(...)-aware tokenizer
body: Batch 20 T2 fix round 1 review, important findings 3-4: the paste-run lint (HR-071) ships with two measured false-positive vehicles, both disclosed as Limits bullets in crates/houserules/src/report_claims.rs rather than narrowed. (1) The appended-annotation check's subshell exemption only covers a `(...)` wrapping the WHOLE command; a chained `cmd1 && (cmd2)` reads as an appended annotation instead — .superpowers/sdd/2026-09-04-batch-17/task-2-report.json live_run[8] is a real instance the shipped checker flags. (2) The placeholder check ignores quote_mask's state entirely, so a quoted angle-bracket literal that is command DATA (an HTML-comment probe, or a `Co-Authored-By: ... <email>` trailer this repository's own standing no-coauthor rule guarantees will keep generating) misreads as a placeholder — the lint's most frequent false positive at filing time: 5 instances across 4 workspace reports.

The narrowing: (a) a quote-aware placeholder arm in find_placeholder, skipping any span quote_mask already marks as inside a quoted string; (b) a $(...)-aware tokenizer arm in quote_mask, tracking that a same-character quote re-opened inside a `$(...)`/`` `...` `` command substitution starts a fresh, independent quoted region rather than closing the one around the whole substitution (the vehicle report_claims.rs's own Limits section discloses from batch 20 T2's first pass, 2 instances in that same review's own corpus sweep). Deferred per process.no-tech-debt: both are bounded, well-scoped engineering — quote_mask already carries the byte-level state the placeholder check would need to consult, and the $(...) arm needs a small quote-context stack, not a rewrite — not a correctness blocker for HR-071's shipped form, which already discloses both gaps with their measured instances rather than shipping them silently.

items.title: release-please misses commits that change the embedded template/ payload but not crates/houserules/**
body: HR-073's release-type: rust at crates/houserules moved release-please's commit attribution off the repository root: CommitSplit.split (commit-split.ts:99) now counts a commit toward the crate's next version only when it touches crates/houserules/**, since the ROOT_PROJECT_PATH special case that used to assign every commit (manifest.ts:700-701) no longer applies. crates/houserules/src/install.rs:232-234 embeds `../../template/` into the shipped binary via #[derive(RustEmbed)], so a commit that changes only template/ (or README.md, or another root-level path) changes shipped code and, under the new attribution, opens no release PR at all.

Measured over v0.2.0-alpha..6aa19e0 (batch 20 T5 fix round 1 review): 82 of 119 commits touch no path under crates/houserules/, and 7 of 27 feat/fix commits are unattributed under the new package path -- four of them (7460c77b feat(template), 6ac1aaa7 fix(template), 719d3f58 fix(tools), 101555ef fix(template)) change the embedded payload directly, per t5-evidence/hr081-template-payload-commits.sh's own enumeration by touched path rather than commit subject (fix round 2: a subject-scoped read of the same range missed 719d3f58, 'fix(tools): validate rejects incomplete terminal reports', which touches no crates/houserules/ path and two template/ files). Today enough crate-side commits ride along that a release PR still opens; a cycle whose only changes are template/, README.md, or the knowledge base would silently ship nothing.

The package path is not the thing to change: release-type rust at '.' (the root) would take the Rust strategy's workspace branch and push a CargoToml update for the root manifest, which cargo-toml.ts:37-40 throws on ('is not a package manifest') since the root Cargo.toml carries no [package] section under this workspace's virtual-manifest shape -- reviewer-confirmed and re-verified by the implementer. The gap needs a different remedy, not a reversal of HR-073's ruling.

Candidate remedies (this item carries the question, not the answer): (a) an extra-files or component-mapping addition to release-please-config.json that attributes template/** changes to the crate's own path for commit-attribution purposes; (b) a documented pre-release rule that a payload-changing commit always rides alongside a crate-side commit before a release is cut, checked by hand or by a gate. Owner picks.

MECHANISM (task-1 fix round 4, provisional pending owner ratification at the batch report): remedy (b), concretized. crates/houserules/payload.stamp records a sha256 digest of template/'s tracked file set, recomputed and compared by payload-stamp-gate (crates/houserules/src/bin/payload-stamp-gate.rs), wired into mise run lint (houserules.payload-stamp-gate). That gate is a TREE-LEVEL check only: a branch splitting the template/ edit from the stamp regeneration across two commits still passes it at the tip. Fix round 5 closed that gap: houserules check-commit now also runs this entry's own co-change check (if template/**, then crates/houserules/payload.stamp) per commit, over the PR's full range in CI, so a split commit pair fails before merge, not only a stale tree.

Still gating this item's own close: the mechanism above is proven by source-level review and a full-pipeline simulation against real git history (batch-24 task-1's own t1-evidence/), never by a genuine release-please run. The first real template-only change that lands on main after T2 -- one commit touching template/ and crates/houserules/payload.stamp together, nothing else -- is that live proof.
Source: batch 20 T5 fix round 1 review (task-5-review.json), important finding 1.

items.title: check-backlog gains a --fix arm for a non-round-tripping backlog file
body: Filed by the task-1 fix round 1 review (minor issue 8): check-backlog's round-trip finding (HR-076) names a concrete remedy per file class, but only backlog/items/*.json has a shipped command that can reach it (`houserules set`). The other five files (schema.json, amendments.json, batches.json, decisions.json, parked.json) have no writer at all, so an adopter who trips this on one of them is told to hand-reproduce serde_json's pretty-printer byte for byte.

Candidate: a `--fix` arm on check-backlog (or a small subcommand) that rewrites the named file through the same `crate::emit::emit` call the check already compares against, so the repair path and the check path stay the same function. Not built in the fix round that filed it: the message-only remedy was the scoped fix; a --fix arm is a larger surface (does it fix every diverging file in one run, or one named file? does it need a --dry-run?) that deserves its own task.

items.title: Main needs the code owner's approval for everyone but the owner; Dependabot auto-merge runs on the owner's token
body: Owner ruling 2026-09-11: only the owner merges to main without an approval; every other contributor's PR needs the owner's approving review. Applied as a second ruleset `approval` on the default branch (one approving review, code-owner review required, stale reviews dismissed on push, threads resolved) whose only bypass actor is the repository admin role. The first ruleset `main` (the eight required checks incl. CodeQL, linear history, no force-push, PR required) keeps no bypass and binds the owner too. GitHub cannot exempt one rule inside a ruleset, hence the split.

Consequence and the ruled fix: GitHub refuses the Actions app as a bypass actor on a user-owned repository, so a merge enabled with GITHUB_TOKEN now waits for an approval and the HR-092 auto-merge stalls. The owner chose the token route: .github/workflows/dependabot-auto-merge.yml enables auto-merge with a fine-grained personal access token of the owner (Contents and Pull requests read/write on this repository only), stored as the Dependabot secret DEPENDABOT_AUTOMERGE_TOKEN (a Dependabot-triggered workflow reads that store, not Actions secrets). A merge performed as the owner also starts the push workflows on main, which lifts HR-092's GITHUB_TOKEN limit for these merges.

PENDING proof: the next minor or patch Dependabot PR merging on its own with the workflow green. Flip to done with that PR's number. HR-068 (a token for the release flow) stays a separate ruling: release-please edits a workflow file, which needs the `workflows` permission this token does not carry.

items.title: macOS signing and notarization in the dist pipeline
body: Deferred at the batch-25 gate (owner, 2026-09-14; design.md 5.79 discharges 5.37's revisit-at-1.0): 1.0 ships unsigned macOS binaries with the current Gatekeeper bypass documented (run once and let macOS block it, then System Settings > Privacy & Security > Open Anyway; amended 2026-09-15, owner ruling - Apple removed right-click-Open in macOS Sequoia). Trigger: real adopter friction with Gatekeeper, not a date. Scope when triggered: the owner's Apple Developer identity and certificates as repository secrets, dist's macos-sign configuration regenerated into release.yml, proven on a watched release.

items.title: check-report-claims: HR-110's locative class ('the X live in Y')
body: Batch 25 T3a shipped only HR-110's number class ('N passed', 'N files' next to a cited capture); the locative class the same item names ('a report narrative stating the X live in Y, citing a retained capture, fails when Y is absent from that capture') is not implemented. The two real batch-23 locative instances that motivated HR-110 both sat in a commit body and a plan file, neither a report-narrative field check-report-claims scans, so this task's own corpus run (every retained deliverable in the tracked tree and the batch workspaces) turned up no report-narrative locative instance to derive a mechanical, low-noise trigger from.

Scoped out per quality.gates-derive-their-scope rather than shipped as a guess: a 'the X live in Y' sentence has no citation-adjacent signal as reliable as HR-110's own digit-token match, and this task's corpus run showed even the number class needs real instances to calibrate against (the 'N files (a, b, c)' enumeration-list false positive, fixed in the same task, only surfaced once real corpus data was run through it). Pick this up once a report-narrative locative instance exists to calibrate against, or once a design session derives a trigger some other way; do not ship an untested heuristic against it.

Rider (batch 25 branch review): report_claims.rs is 2889 lines - before this item (or HR-124) lands there, split the three checks and the shared resolver into submodules per the batch-25 plan's god-file direction.

items.title: check-report-claims: HR-111's multi-file sweep-coverage case
body: Batch 25 T3a fix round 1: check_narrative_sweep_coverage (HR-111) returns early unless a report's files_changed names exactly one file. Measured over the task's own 350-file corpus (t3a-files-changed-reach.py, retained at .superpowers/sdd/2026-09-14-batch-25/): 3 of 350 deliverables carry exactly one files_changed entry (where the check runs), 93 carry more than one, 3 carry an empty files_changed array, and the remaining 251 are review kinds that carry no files_changed field at all -- so the check is inert on 347 of 350 retained deliverables, the common case by a wide margin.

Blocker: this task's corpus run found no reliable signal for WHICH of several changed files a given sweep/enumeration citation is offered as proof for. Comparing a sweep's content against the WHOLE files_changed list once produced a flood of false positives (a narrowly-scoped sweep has no reason to mention a plan file or a schema copy the same task also edited); a two-citation-per-sentence heuristic (the sweep, then a second citation naming the certified file) would have missed the task's own real motivating instance (HR-111's own origin, batch 23 T1: the sentence names only the sweep, relying on the reader knowing which file the task is about). Picking this up needs either a design session to derive a real per-file attribution signal, or a corpus of real multi-file sweep citations large enough to calibrate one against -- this task's own corpus supplied none.
Origin: batch 25 T3a (HR-111); this item schedules the deferred multi-file case rather than leaving it only as a report concern, per process.no-tech-debt.
Rider (batch 25 branch review): see HR-123's split-first note - the same file hosts both items.

items.title: Vacuousness check for dist-workspace.toml's [dist.github-action-commits] seed table
body: Batch 25 T4 review (reproduced by the reviewer): the seed table is a third exception-shaped list with no vacuousness check - an entry naming an action dist never emits (probe: appending 'actions/never-emitted-by-dist') passes dist-generate-check silently, and the four seeded actions' sha values are by construction of the reseed never compared against anything by that gate (a zeroed 'actions/attest' sha also exits 0). Same class HR-115's vacuous-exception-gate covers for the tree's other two exception-list shapes. Fix: assert every seed-table action appears in dist's generated release.yml (and consider the sha-column direction), in the gate or beside it.

items.title: Deterministic verify-drift warn: a changed verify-listed file flags its entry for re-read
body: Batch 25 branch review: state-only-the-source was the batch's most-violated rule (7 counts + 1 live at the review) - prose describing a mechanism goes stale when a fix round changes the mechanism. Add an audit warn row: when a range changes a file named in an entry's verify list without touching that entry's own topic file, flag the entry ('verify-drift'). Proof case: cite-durable-refs' body described the rejected --base design after 0864f1a changed durable_sha.rs, which its verify names.

items.title: check-report-claims covers reviews; closure-word lint
body: Batch 25 branch review, two arms. (a) Reviews quote counts and outputs like reports do (4 claims-match counts this batch, 3 critical): run check-report-claims over review deliverables and add its clean run to the task-reviewer template's closing act like the implementer template mandates. (b) Closure-word lint: a narrative field containing every/all/no remaining/zero without a named artifact or command in the same field is flagged (4 closure-claim counts this batch; HR-124 books the sweep-coverage widening separately).

items.title: Template-cluster riders from the batch-25 branch review
body: Four defects for the next template-touching batch. (1) task-reviewer template: an issue that cites a rule flips that rule's rule_adherence row to fail in the same review - or stats additionally tallies issues[].rule and new_breakage[].rule (this batch: stats reports 13 violated ids where the 14 reviews yield 20). (2) deliverables schema (both copies, parity-pinned): an optional fix_rounds[].gates_run field so the audit can flag a fix round that never re-ran the full mirror set (3 shrunken-gate-list instances this batch). (3) the orchestrating skill's dispatch checklist: a brief that forbids tree changes names the controller as the homing path for deferrals (T1's structural rulings-to-file breach). (4) task-reviewer fix-round section: a fix round records the FULL mirror set; a shrunken tests list is an automatic re-review finding.

items.title: check-knowledge lint: a rule-kind entry without a loading path
body: Batch 25 branch review: an adopted rule landed in an area whose globs no longer covered the files it governs, caught only by judged review. Deterministic floor: flag a rule-kind entry whose standing is false and whose area globs match no tracked file class it names (exact predicate to be designed against areas.json's shape).

items.title: durable-sha's default-branch resolution vs exotic adopter defaults - owner ruling needed
body: Batch 25 T3b/branch review: durable-sha hard-fails (named exit 2) for an adopter whose default branch is neither main nor master and who lacks an origin/HEAD symref - the designed, named behavior. Any repair (a flag, a config key) lands under houserules.1-0-surface-is-frozen after the cut, so the fix needs an owner ruling either way. OWNER RULING NEEDED before scheduling.

items.title: README rework: research-derived structure, adopter-first, evidence narration stripped
body: Owner direction (2026-09-15): research what a good open-source README is, derive the ideal structure for this repo before consulting the current file, compare, then rework completely. Owner-triaged rulings: strip ALL maintainer-evidence narration (Live-verified blocks, HR-refs, design.md cites, checked-dates, the moot mise minimum_release_age forensic - provenance stays in specs/knowledge); the convergence thesis becomes a short plain-claims Why section; ADD a ToC, a CLI reference table (the 20 frozen subcommands, replacing the misleading pipe-notation Daily commands block), a Stability/1.0-contract section, and a Contributing & support section; Updating folds under Install. Process deviation ruled for this batch only: no spec, no implementer/reviewer - the controller researches, presents, triages with the owner, and does the rework itself (design.md 5.84).
Scope addition (owner, 2026-09-15): the README also states how houserules can be uninstalled, as convenience information for users.

items.title: houserules update self-updates the installed binary
body: Owner (2026-09-15): 'houserules update does update a repo but it doesn't update the installed houserules binary. It should.' Design at spec time: the mechanism must respect the install channel (shell installer, mise, direct download) - a mise-managed binary is mise's to update, a self-replaced one needs the dist install receipt. Cluster with HR-134 and HR-135.

items.title: Update-available notice on every command when a newer release exists
body: Owner (2026-09-15): when a new houserules version is published, the binary states that an update is available on every command, as a small header, like other CLI tools do. Design at spec time: version check against the GitHub latest release with a local cache and a short TTL; never a network call per invocation; silent on network failure; an opt-out env var. Cluster with HR-133 and HR-135.

items.title: Install path: does ~/.cargo/bin make sense for a toolchain-neutral binary?
body: Owner (2026-09-15): houserules currently installs into .cargo; 'I am asking myself if that makes sense for a pure binary that has nothing to do with rust anymore on the user systems.' The shell installer's target comes from dist-workspace.toml (cargo-dist install-path; CARGO_HOME is the default). Candidate: ~/.local/bin (XDG) with a PATH fallback. Needs an owner ruling; a move also needs a migration story for existing installs and feeds HR-133's self-update mechanism. Cluster with HR-133 and HR-134.
